svg.text: Four independent observations, all pointing away from the same explanation

g.data-tip: The paper argues this optimization difficulty is unlikely to be caused by vanishing gradients, and gives four separate reasons. Vanishing gradients were the obstacle before this paper, and the introduction says they had been largely addressed by normalized initialization and intermediate normalization layers.
g.text: Deep plain nets fail because the gradient vanishes on the way back, and the shortcut gives it a highway

g.data-tip: Section 3.4: batch normalisation is adopted right after each convolution and before activation, in the plain networks as well as the residual ones. That is what keeps the forward signal alive.

Section 4.1, in one sentence: the authors verify that the backward propagated gradients exhibit healthy norms with BN, and conclude that neither forward nor backward signals vanish. No plot, number or definition of healthy is given, so this is the weakest of the four observations.

g.data-tiphead: The plain net is not dead
g.data-tip: A network whose gradients had vanished would not learn at all. plain-34 reaches accuracy in the same range as VGG-16, which the paper reads as the solver working to some extent.
g.text: would not train at all. This

g.data-tip: Footnote 3: the authors experimented with three times more training iterations and still observed the degradation problem, so it cannot feasibly be addressed by simply training for longer.

a.data-tip: Section 4.1 ends with a conjecture, not an explanation: the deep plain nets may have exponentially low convergence rates, which impact the reducing of the training error. The reason for such optimization difficulties will be studied in the future.
a.text: So what does the paper put in its place? A conjecture, and an open question
It conjectures that the deep plain nets may have exponentially low convergence rates, which impact the reducing of the training error,
and then says plainly that the reason for such optimization difficulties will be studied in the future.
Read the conjecture as: training error keeps falling, but so slowly that no feasible schedule reaches the shallower net — footnote 3 tried 3x the iterations.
Worth being blunt about: this paper demonstrates that residual learning fixes degradation. It does not explain why degradation
happens, and it explicitly declines the explanation almost everyone repeats.
